questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design a per-tenant provenance flow, integrate image signing and SBOMs, and apply admission controls with policy-as-code. It also checks practical knowledge of Gatekeeper/OPA integration, namespace-scoped policies, and minimal test workflows.

## Key Concepts

- Cosign signing with tenant-specific keys
- SPDX SBOM attachment and verification
- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- Per-tenant policy in a ConfigMap
- Minimal manifests and kubectl validation in a single namespace

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (yaml)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8simageprovenance
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sImageProvenance
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8simageprovenance
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Deployment"
        some c in input.review.object.spec.template.spec.containers
        not startswith(c.image, "ghcr.io/")
        msg := "image provenance missing or not tenant-approved"
      }
```

```yaml
# Constraint (yaml)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sImageProvenance
metadata:
  name: per-tenant-provenance
spec:
  enforcementAction: deny
  parameters:
    allowedTenant: "tenant-a"
```

```yaml
# Compliant Deployment (yaml)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: ghcr.io/tenant-a/gateway:v1.0.0
```

```yaml
# Noncompliant Deployment (yaml)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-gateway-bad
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: unsigned/gateway:latest
```

```bash
# Kubectl steps (one namespace first)
kubectl create ns tenant-a
# 1) Register constraint template and constraint
kubectl apply -f k8simageprovenance_template.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8simageprovenance_constraint.yaml
# 2) Sign and SBOM-attach a valid image (tenant-a key)
cosign sign --key cosign-tenant-a.key ghcr.io/tenant-a/gateway:v1.0.0
# 3) Deploy compliant manifest
kubectl apply -f compliant-deploy.yaml -n tenant-a
# 4) Deploy noncompliant manifest (unsigned)
kubectl apply -f noncompliant-deploy.yaml -n tenant-a
# 5) Check Gatekeeper denials and logs
kubectl get events -n tenant-a
kubectl describe deployment tenant-a-gateway-bad -n tenant-a
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you rotate tenant keys without downtime?
- How would you extend to multi-tenant namespaces concurrently?

questions.explanation:
Why This Is Asked
- Tests reliability patterns in CNF deployments. 
- Exercises understanding of the sidecar pattern, process supervision, and per-tenant isolation.
- Checks how backoff, crash loops, and health endpoints are wired in Kubernetes.

Key Concepts
- Process supervision and exit handling in a container.
- Per-tenant state via labels/annotations and isolated metrics.
- Liveness/readiness semantics and crash-loop protection.

Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
  labels:
    app: cnf-gateway
    tenant: <tenant-id>
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cnf-gateway
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cnf-gateway
        tenant: <tenant-id>
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: cnf-main
          image: cnf/main:latest
        - name: watchdog
          image: cnf/watchdog:latest
          env:
            - name: CNF_MAIN_BIN
              value: "/cnf/main/bin/cnf"
          volumeMounts:
            - mountPath: "/cnf/main/bin"
              name: bin
      volumes:
        - name: bin
          emptyDir: {}
```

Follow-up Questions
- How would you add jitter to the backoff to avoid thundering herd? 
- How would you test crash-loop protection in CI/CD?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates practical knowledge of cross-tenant isolation using runtime attestation (SPIRE) and policy enforcement (OPA) in CNF meshes. It assesses understanding of real-world challenges including tenant scoping, short-lived credential management, and gateway security enforcement.

## Key Concepts
- SPIRE workload attestation and SVID binding to tenant ID
- OPA/Rego policy enforcement for tenant isolation
- Service mesh RBAC, namespaces, and tenant-scoped ServiceAccounts
- End-to-end testing within a single namespace

## Code Example
```yaml
# SPIRE Attestation
apiVersion: spire.spiffe.io/v1alpha1
kind: ClusterSPIFFEID
metadata:
  name: cnf-workload
spec:
  spiffeIDTemplate: "spiffe://example.com/ns/{namespace}/tenant/{tenant_id}"
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cnf
  tenantIDLabel: "tenant.id"
---
# OPA Authorization Policy
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-gateway-policy
  namespace: istio-system
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: istio-ingressgateway
  action: CUSTOM
  provider:
    name: opa
  rules:
  - when:
    - key: request.headers[x-spire-attestation]
      notValues: ["invalid"]
    - key: request.headers[x-tenant-capability]
      values: ["tenant-a-read", "tenant-a-write"]
---
# Test Manifest (single namespace)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-a
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: cnf-workload
  namespace: tenant-a
  labels:
    tenant.id: "tenant-a"
    tenant.capability: "read,write"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: cnf-api
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  selector:
    app: cnf
  ports:
  - port: 8080
    targetPort: 8080
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question validates the ability to design per-tenant request mutation with runtime configuration, isolation, and safe rollback—a realistic pattern in CNF gateways deploying WASM filters.

## Key Concepts
- WASM sandboxing and module loading in a CNF sidecar
- Tenant-scoped policy storage with fast reloads via ConfigMap
- Validation, rollback, and observability in a live gateway
- End-to-end testing using a one-namespace manifest

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf.filter.rules
  namespace: cnf-gateway
data:
  rules.json: |
    {
      "tenant1:abc123": {
        "pathRewrite": {
          "pattern": "^/v1/(.*)$",
          "replacement": "/tenant1/v1/$1"
        },
        "headers": {
          "add": {
            "X-Forwarded-Tenant": "tenant1",
            "X-Tenant-ID": "tenant1"
          }
        }
      }
    }
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
  namespace: cnf-gateway
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
  namespace: cnf-gateway
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cnf-gateway
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cnf-gateway
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: cnf-gateway
      containers:
      - name: proxy
        image: envoyproxy/envoy:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: wasm-filter
          mountPath: /etc/wasm-filters
        - name: rules
          mountPath: /etc/config
        env:
        - name: CONFIG_MAP_NAME
          value: cnf.filter.rules
      volumes:
      - name: wasm-filter
        emptyDir: {}
      - name: rules
        configMap:
          name: cnf.filter.rules
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical runtime network security for multi-tenant CNF gateways, requiring hands-on knowledge of Cilium, Kubernetes NetworkPolicies, DNS controls, and observability in a distributed environment.

## Key Concepts
- CiliumNetworkPolicy
- NetworkPolicy basics
- tenantID labeling
- per-tenant DNS allowlists
- observability with cilium policy trace

## Code Example
```yaml
# CiliumNetworkPolicy isolating by tenantID
apiVersion: "cilium.io/v2"
kind: CiliumNetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-isolation
  namespace: cnf-gws
spec:
  endpointSelector:
    matchLabels:
      tenantID: "tA"
  ingress:
  - from:
    - sourceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          tenantID: "tA"
  egress:
  - toEndpoints:
    - matchLabels:
        tenantID: "tA"
```
```yaml
# Kubernetes NetworkPolicy for per-tenant gateway
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-tenant-gateway
  namespace: cnf-gws
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      tenantID: "tA"
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.1.0.0/16
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question probes practical runtime config at scale, emphasizing isolation, zero-downtime updates, auditability, and integration with existing gateway proxies.

## Key Concepts
- Runtime feature flags per tenant
- Streaming update mechanism with local caching
- RBAC, audit logging, and change-tracking
- Minimal manifest demonstrating flag toggling

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: cnf.example/v1
kind: FeatureFlag
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-flags
  namespace: cnf-tenant-a
spec:
  tenantID: tenant-a
  flags:
    enableBurst: true
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you rotate the feature-flag backend and ensure no traffic drop during failover?
- How would you correlate flag changes with traffic telemetry for troubleshooting?
